brain.name: FP&A Commercial
brain.scope: From Brand Manager revenue assumptions to the signed-off P&L and its control attestation: revenue, manpower, non-manpower and CAPEX planning, P&L consolidation and PMR submission with CMR validation, the planning deck, pre-close analysis, monthly revenue and cost reporting, the mid-month forecast and the FCF controls in FAST+. Pain points and activity types reflect the updated As-Is map reviewed with FP&A Commercial.
meta: FP&A Commercial (GFS KL) with CP, CFO, BUDs, Brand Managers, HR, Embedded Finance and International
Annual plan cycles (RBU, MTP, Budget); monthly pre-close, reporting, mid-month forecast and FCF attestation
Excel on SharePoint, SAP (MM60, FBL3N, GD13), PMR / CMR, AZ FORCE, Cost Tool, CAS (CAPEX), Power BI, FAST+, OneGRC

ai.t: AI-generated approval pack summary
ai.d: Create a concise, cited summary of the submitted evidence and key variances for the approver, while leaving the approval decision with the named person.

ai.t: AI prediction of approval bottlenecks
ai.d: Use historical cycle times, leave patterns and queue load to flag requests likely to miss the cut-off and prompt earlier delegation.

ai.t: AI-assisted duplicate and evidence-reuse check
ai.d: Identify duplicate requests and previously approved evidence that may be valid for the same market, control and period, subject to owner confirmation.

ai.t: Natural-language approval pipeline Q&A
ai.d: Allow authorised users to ask which markets are outstanding, where requests are blocked and which approver owns the next action, with links to the underlying requests.

ai.t: AI first-level variance screening with a moving threshold
ai.d: AI picks the brands, cost centres and GLs above a threshold set to the size of the variance, e.g. 10k or 30–50k. Hackathon output.

ai.t: AI agent on the P&L for CFO, business partners and country president
ai.d: Leaders prompt for the main drivers, e.g. sales deterioration versus latest forecast, once the P&L is final.

ai.t: Materiality rule held as a table, not chosen by eye
ai.d: Set the threshold by rule, e.g. % of total variance or Pareto 80%. AI then explains only the items that pass.

ai.t: AI draft commentary with transaction evidence
ai.d: Draft the variance explanation from the top PO and vendor lines behind each flagged item, for analyst approval.

ai.t: Work with the hackathon team on the AI screening design
ai.d: FP&A told the hackathon team the tool must serve the P&L while it is still open, not only once it is final.

mapHypotheses.t: Planning calendar with agreed cut-offs per market
mapHypotheses.d: Fix the revenue planning calendar and cut-offs with the market after the Business Strategy Meetings, reducing idle time between alignment discussions.
mapHypotheses.where: Stage 1: Revenue Planning by SKU and Brand

mapHypotheses.t: AI baseline volume per SKU for Brand Managers
mapHypotheses.d: A statistical baseline per SKU from the phased actuals is pre-filled for Brand Managers, who adjust it with their assumptions; fewer revision cycles start from a blank template.
mapHypotheses.where: Stage 1: Revenue Planning by SKU and Brand · Revenue Planning

mapHypotheses.t: One planning intake for MPC, NMPC and CAPEX
mapHypotheses.d: One SharePoint / Power Apps intake hub for brand FTE, cost centre and CAPEX inputs with shared reminders and a status view for FP&A and Market Finance.
mapHypotheses.where: Stage 2: Manpower (MPC), Non-Manpower (NMPC) & CAPEX Planning

mapHypotheses.t: Brand-level FTE field in AZ FORCE
mapHypotheses.d: Raise a change request for brand-level FTE input in AZ FORCE, so brand allocation is captured in the planning system instead of a side Excel collection.
mapHypotheses.where: Stage 2: Manpower (MPC), Non-Manpower (NMPC) & CAPEX Planning · MPC Planning (Manpower Cost Planning)

mapHypotheses.t: AI anomaly screening of cost centre inputs
mapHypotheses.d: A model trained on prior cycles and actuals flags unusual cost lines before the FP&A review, focusing the review loop.
mapHypotheses.where: Stage 2: Manpower (MPC), Non-Manpower (NMPC) & CAPEX Planning · NMPC Planning (Non-Manpower Cost Planning)

mapHypotheses.t: CAPEX planning tool with an embedded approval flow
mapHypotheses.d: The improvement named in the CAPEX planning summary: one tool for business input, CBP review, CFO approval and the Region submission, replacing template cascades by email.
mapHypotheses.where: Stage 2: Manpower (MPC), Non-Manpower (NMPC) & CAPEX Planning · CAPEX Planning

mapHypotheses.t: Reduce the key-person dependency on the master P&L model
mapHypotheses.d: Document the model (tab map, inputs vs logic, run steps) and rotate a trained back-up through each cycle.
mapHypotheses.where: Stage 3: P&L Planning & Total Company Consolidation

mapHypotheses.t: AI-drafted P&L bridge between iterations
mapHypotheses.d: Copilot drafts the bridge between P&L iterations (what changed by brand and P&L line, and why) for the CFO / CP alignment.
mapHypotheses.where: Stage 3: P&L Planning & Total Company Consolidation · P&L Planning

mapHypotheses.t: Agreed input cut-off with Embedded Finance
mapHypotheses.d: A fixed cut-off for Embedded Finance files per iteration, with changes after it going to the next iteration.
mapHypotheses.where: Stage 4: Planning System Submission & PMR-CMR Validation

mapHypotheses.t: One validation suite for the PMR submission
mapHypotheses.d: Conso Check, PMR load, PMR vs Analytics and PMR vs CMR run as one scripted suite per iteration with a single exceptions report.
mapHypotheses.where: Stage 4: Planning System Submission & PMR-CMR Validation · Planning System Submission

mapHypotheses.t: Deck-aligned international template released on a fixed date
mapHypotheses.d: Agree with International Finance a locked template that matches the deck, released on a fixed date per cycle.
mapHypotheses.where: Stage 5: Planning Deck Preparation & Leadership Review

mapHypotheses.t: Copilot draft of the deck narrative
mapHypotheses.d: Copilot drafts the key messages per slide from the refreshed numbers for FP&A to edit.
mapHypotheses.where: Stage 5: Planning Deck Preparation & Leadership Review · Planning Review Preparation (Planning Deck Preparation)

mapHypotheses.t: Root-cause log of correction requests
mapHypotheses.d: Log pre-close correction requests by root cause (wrong cost centre, missing accrual, wrong period) and share a monthly summary with the booking teams, so repeat errors are prevented.
mapHypotheses.where: Stage 6: Pre-Close Analysis

mapHypotheses.t: Bring known accruals into the pre-close view
mapHypotheses.d: Late costs advised informally by Embedded Finance and known accrual lists show as expected postings, so fewer variances need a query.
mapHypotheses.where: Stage 6: Pre-Close Analysis · Pre-close Analysis

mapHypotheses.t: Standard revenue and cost output structure across markets
mapHypotheses.d: Agree a common core structure for the revenue and cost outputs with market-specific add-ons, so scripts and dashboards can be reused.
mapHypotheses.where: Stage 7: Monthly Revenue & Cost Reporting

mapHypotheses.t: Python build of the 37-tab revenue master
mapHypotheses.d: One scripted run builds the revenue master from SAP and CMR extracts with the reconciliation, rules and checks above.
mapHypotheses.where: Stage 7: Monthly Revenue & Cost Reporting · Revenue Reporting

mapHypotheses.t: SAP-CMR reconciliation page on the RLS dashboard
mapHypotheses.d: Show the SAP vs CMR reconciliation and stale FX / uplift values on the cost dashboard, so discrepancies are visible to everyone using it.
mapHypotheses.where: Stage 7: Monthly Revenue & Cost Reporting · Cost Reporting

mapHypotheses.t: Decouple forecast collection from the month-end peak
mapHypotheses.d: Start BUD collection on a flash of prior-month sales and refresh actuals once final, so MMF does not collide with month-end close.
mapHypotheses.where: Stage 8: Mid-Month / Rolling Forecast

mapHypotheses.t: AI baseline sales forecast for BUD review
mapHypotheses.d: A run-rate and seasonality baseline per brand is pre-filled so BUDs forecast the delta, reducing routine rework.
mapHypotheses.where: Stage 8: Mid-Month / Rolling Forecast · Mid-Month Forecast (MMF)

mapHypotheses.t: Standard evidence pack per FSC control
mapHypotheses.d: Define the minimum evidence set for FSC008, FSC009 and FSC011 as a checklist in FAST+ across the 14 markets.
mapHypotheses.where: Stage 9: FCF Control Attestation via FAST+

mapHypotheses.t: Power BI control status across 14 markets
mapHypotheses.d: Submission, approval, delegation and OneGRC upload status by market and control (FSC008, FSC009, FSC011) in one view.
mapHypotheses.where: Stage 9: FCF Control Attestation via FAST+ · FCF Control on Revenue and P&L (FAST+)

pancreas.scope: From the planning target and the published production volume to the signed-off Group planning submission, and from the month-end close to the regional MI Pack and the leadership insights: volume & COGM, logistics, workforce & OPEX, CAPEX, product costing and inventory planning, productivity bridges and site packs, reviews and sign-off, month-end actualization, variance analysis and performance reporting. The two LT feedback decks (Planning and Actual) are applied: Cost & Resource Planning merged into Operational Planning, Commentary Generation consolidated into Performance Reporting, boxes removed, combined and renamed and pain points revised as marked.
meta: FP&A Ops (GFS KL) with Embedded Finance (EF), Global Ops, GSC&S, PC CoE, CAPEX, Global Logistics Finance, HR, Site CFOs / RFDs and the Global Reporting Team
Every planning cycle (e.g. RBU, Phased Budget); monthly close WD1–WD+5 with the MI Pack and regional consolidation
Hyperion (Planning Hub / OPS Cube / OPSPR), AZForce, Capex Tool / CAPROW, CAS, GSC&S BP Portal, BPP, FDH, SAP, SOAR / BW, OBIEE / ASO, Power BI, Lean P&L, AI Agent Rhy

ai.t: AI-assisted variance commentary
ai.d: Draft first-pass commentary from actuals, comparators, planning assumptions and validated exceptions, then route it to the responsible finance reviewer for approval.
ai.feas: Can be implemented in the future
ai.feasc:
Reviewed and aligned with futher input.

A like-for-like comparison between Actuals and Planning may be challenging with the current dataset for the following reasons:
1. Different levels of granularity: Actuals are available at the general ledger (GL) level, whereas Planning data is maintained at a higher level, such as the WRAP level.
2. Planning assumptions are not captured: The underlying assumptions used for the Planning figures are not currently stored in the dashboard, which limits the ability to explain or reconcile variances.

ai.t: AI commentary and decision-support guardrails
ai.d: Document that AI can explain, summarise and validate but cannot own finance conclusions; require source citations, reviewer approval, prompt/version control and retained output history.
ai.feasc:
Reviewed and aligned with further input

The AI commentary might only be able to generate relevant decision-support insights when sufficient planning granularity and the underlying planning assumptions are available (as mentioned under FPA-12).

mapHypotheses.t: One planning intake for targets, volumes and system openings
mapHypotheses.d: A single planning intake page lists the target release, the volume publication and the system openings with their dates and owners, so every stream starts from the same published inputs.
mapHypotheses.where: Demand & Operational Inputs · Planning Inputs & Cycle Kick-off

mapHypotheses.t: One planning calendar and exception view across the six Operational Planning streams
mapHypotheses.d: Volume & COGM, logistics, workforce & OPEX, CAPEX, product costing and inventory share one calendar of loads and sign-offs and one exception view, so the stretch timeline and the multiple information feeds are managed centrally.
mapHypotheses.where: Operational Planning

mapHypotheses.t: COGM calculation run as a monitored job with ESM ownership
mapHypotheses.d: The OPS Cube COGM calculation is scheduled after the final volume load with a completion and FMC-gap report to the named ESM COGM owner, EF and the GFS SME.
mapHypotheses.where: Operational Planning · Operations Planning – Volume & Cost of Goods Manufactured modelling

mapHypotheses.t: Logistics planning driver model shared with GLF
mapHypotheses.d: Primary and secondary distribution drivers (rates, volumes, DC capacity, savings) in one governed model used by the APAC and GLF reviews, so the consolidation reviews work from the same assumptions.
mapHypotheses.where: Operational Planning · Global Logistic & Warehouse

mapHypotheses.t: AZForce and OPS Cube actualisation on one FX version
mapHypotheses.d: Align the actualisation timing and exchange-rate version between AZForce and Ops Cube Hyperion so artificial USD variances no longer need repeated manual correction.
mapHypotheses.where: Operational Planning · Workforce & OPEX Planning

mapHypotheses.t: CAPEX planning intake linked to CAS
mapHypotheses.d: One intake for project templates with the CAS approved funding and T-code status attached, giving EF, the CAPEX analysts and the RFDs the same view of each project.
mapHypotheses.where: Operational Planning · CAPEX Planning

mapHypotheses.t: Inventory planning exceptions dashboard
mapHypotheses.d: Mapping gaps, price gaps, BPP-to-Planning-Hub differences and provision anomalies on one Power BI page for the Inventory team, EF and GSC&S Finance.
mapHypotheses.where: Operational Planning · Inventory Planning

mapHypotheses.t: Cost-base handover from Planning Hub to the costing run
mapHypotheses.d: Site and Global Quality expenses, Central OH and distribution and warehouse costs are passed to PC CoE as a reconciled extract from Planning Hub rather than assembled by hand.
mapHypotheses.where: Operational Planning · Product Costing (FMC & SCC)

mapHypotheses.t: Site pack and bridge Q&A agent for site finance
mapHypotheses.d: A Copilot agent over the site P&L, packs and productivity bridges answers site and RFD questions during the review window with source references.
mapHypotheses.where: P&L Modelling & Forecasting

mapHypotheses.t: Productivity bridge pre-filled from OPS Cube
mapHypotheses.d: The CY / CY+1 bridge opens pre-filled with the COGM and M&O movements from Planning Hub and the ESM component values, leaving the drivers and initiatives for the site to complete.
mapHypotheses.where: P&L Modelling & Forecasting · Productivity Planning & Cost per Unit

mapHypotheses.t: Site pack and Steerco tracker on linked data
mapHypotheses.d: The site output pack and the planning activity tracker read the planning systems directly, so the pack refreshes with the numbers and the Steerco sees live adherence.
mapHypotheses.where: P&L Modelling & Forecasting · Site P&L and Review Packs

mapHypotheses.t: Review-cycle assistant extending Agent Charlie
mapHypotheses.d: Agent Charlie in Copilot Studio also tracks review actions and post-review adjustments across sites and drafts the follow-up list after each review.
mapHypotheses.where: Planning Review and Sign-Off

mapHypotheses.t: Agent Charlie for the planning review cycle
mapHypotheses.d: Agent Charlie gives the site cheat sheets for the site reviews and the regional headline by cost category for the regional packs, with the analysts validating every draft (register RHY-05, RHY-06).
mapHypotheses.where: Planning Review and Sign-Off · Planning Review and Sign-Off (Site → Region → Group)

mapHypotheses.t: Coupa accrual lines enriched with PO text for Ops
mapHypotheses.d: R2R passes the PO text with the Coupa accrual JE posting so the Ops analyst can explain the accrual variances; raised as a cross-tower request with R2R and P2P.
mapHypotheses.where: Month-End Actualization

mapHypotheses.t: Close built on the Finance Data Hub staging layer
mapHypotheses.d: Pre-close checks, the P&L Review file and the final reconciliation read one governed staging layer with automated SAP vs ASO reconciliation, removing the multi-system rebuild during close (register FPA-03, FPA-06, FPA-15).
mapHypotheses.where: Month-End Actualization · Month-End Close: Pre-close, Journals & SAP Close

mapHypotheses.t: Shared variance-screening logic with the FP&A P&L Data House project
mapHypotheses.d: One threshold rule set for site and market commentary so Ops and Commercial variance commentary read the same way (register RHY-29).
mapHypotheses.where: Variance Analysis

mapHypotheses.t: Rule-based variance extraction with AI first-layer review
mapHypotheses.d: Variances are extracted by rule from the governed dashboards, screened for anomalies and stored as a driver table, so the analyst's time goes to explaining drivers (register FPA-10, RHY-12, RHY-17).
mapHypotheses.where: Variance Analysis · Variance Analysis vs Budget / RBU

mapHypotheses.t: Volume commentary pulled forward to WD+1 with Global Supply Chain
mapHypotheses.d: GFS sends the key brands to NSP on WD-4, NSP inputs by end WD-1 and GFS drafts for site finance on WD+2, with a threshold or Pareto rule for the brands needing commentary (register RHY-22, RHY-23, RHY-24).
mapHypotheses.where: Performance Reporting

mapHypotheses.t: AI-assisted commentary with guardrails and evidence check
mapHypotheses.d: First-pass commentary drafted from the driver table, captured through Power Apps, checked against the dashboard measures and approved by the responsible reviewer under documented guardrails (register FPA-09, FPA-12, FPA-13, FPA-23).
mapHypotheses.where: Performance Reporting · Commentary Preparation

mapHypotheses.t: Agent Rhy as the APAC consolidation standard, reused across regions and towers
mapHypotheses.d: A hardened Rhy run (completeness, version guard, trigger, totals check, run log) with the pattern offered to other Ops regions and to towers that summarise many documents (register RHY-28, RHY-32).
mapHypotheses.where: Performance Reporting · MI Pack Review & Sign-Off (Site and Regional)

mapHypotheses.t: Leadership Q&A agent over the MI Pack and Flash
mapHypotheses.d: A Copilot agent grounded on the approved regional MI Pack and Flash lets leadership ask questions on movements and risks with evidence from the pack.
mapHypotheses.where: Leadership Insights & Decision Support

mapHypotheses.t: Earlier APAC view for the Global Ops close
mapHypotheses.d: The automated regional consolidation supports the Global Ops close at WD+6 in 2026 and WD+5 in 2027, on the path to WD+3 by 2030 (register RHY-25).
mapHypotheses.where: Leadership Insights & Decision Support · Leadership Insights & Decision Support

mapHypotheses.t: Capital approval tracker by stage
mapHypotheses.d: Power BI view of proposals by stage (drafted, CAB review, DOA in CAS, code requested, code created) with ageing per stage, so the Business and Local Finance see where approvals sit instead of asking by email.
mapHypotheses.where: Capital Project Approval & Set-up · Review and Approve Capital Projects

mapHypotheses.t: CAS-to-SAP project set-up in one flow
mapHypotheses.d: Approval in CAS triggers the WBSE and budget template for DMT, the automated CAS-vs-SAP validation for Local Finance and the CAS update with the new code - one tracked flow instead of five handoffs by email.
mapHypotheses.where: Capital Project Approval & Set-up · Create Project Account Codes

mapHypotheses.t: AUC ageing and capitalisation backlog dashboard
mapHypotheses.d: Power BI on AUC balances by project and age with the capitalisation and closure status, so long-outstanding AUC is capitalised or impaired on time; the same view gives FP&A the actual capex spend vs plan the register proposes as a link.
mapHypotheses.feasc: Register GFA-26 budget vs capitalised actual view and GFA-29 CapEx utilisation check are Feasible.
mapHypotheses.where: Project Spend, Settlement & Capitalisation

mapHypotheses.t: Project spend exception monitoring
mapHypotheses.d: Scheduled script over the monthly CJI3 postings flags out-of-scope spend, over-budget WBSEs and settlement-rule gaps before the settlement run; Local Finance and CAPEX work the exceptions in one list.
mapHypotheses.where: Project Spend, Settlement & Capitalisation · Record Project Related Transactions

mapHypotheses.t: Closure-candidate detection and capitalisation checklist
mapHypotheses.d: Rule-based closure candidates from CN41N / AR02 plus an auto-populated commitment checklist (open PO, T&E, CATS) so projects are capitalised when complete rather than when noticed.
mapHypotheses.where: Project Spend, Settlement & Capitalisation · Close and Capitalise Projects

mapHypotheses.t: Asset request to asset code workflow
mapHypotheses.d: Power Apps request with CAS approval check, AS01 upload for DMT, automatic notification and tag request, monthly unposted-asset follow-up with a response tracker.
mapHypotheses.where: Fixed Asset Additions · Process and Record Fixed Asset Additions - Commercial

mapHypotheses.t: Depreciation run control tower
mapHypotheses.d: Scheduled test run, classified error list with owners, automated variance check with thresholds, Copilot-drafted explanations, go / no-go and scheduled production run - with run status per company code in Power BI.
mapHypotheses.where: Depreciation & Amortisation · Calculate and Record Depreciation Expense

mapHypotheses.t: Impairment indicator screening
mapHypotheses.d: Candidate list for the annual impairment review built from asset movement, cost centre status, cancelled projects and physical verification results, with the accounting treatment proposed per candidate for Local Finance to confirm.
mapHypotheses.where: Impairments, Retirements & Transfers · Process and Record Fixed Asset Impairments

mapHypotheses.t: Retirement and transfer request workflow with DOA routing
mapHypotheses.d: Form pre-filled from AS03, route determined by rule (transfer within entity, class change, between entities, decommission, sale), DOA approvals and the DMT / CAPEX actions tracked in one record.
mapHypotheses.where: Impairments, Retirements & Transfers · Process and Record Fixed Asset Retirements

mapHypotheses.t: Digital physical verification
mapHypotheses.d: Asset lists generated per point of contact, mobile verification form with barcode scan, automatic reminders and a Power BI status view that feeds DMT master data updates and the impairment review.
mapHypotheses.where: Physical Asset Verification · Track Fixed Assets including Physical Inventory

mapHypotheses.t: Lease cycle status board (WD-8 to WD-1)
mapHypotheses.d: Power BI status of the lease cycle per entity: DCTs received, ETL uploads, records pending review, open alerts, journals exported and BlackLine acknowledgement - so the Global Lease Team and Local Finance see the critical path to WD-1 journals.
mapHypotheses.where: Lease Accounting (IFRS 16)

mapHypotheses.t: Validated lease data collection
mapHypotheses.d: Data Collection Template validated against SAP master data at entry and mapped to the ETL template by script, removing most ETL upload errors and the master data loop (8.3.3.16).
mapHypotheses.where: Lease Accounting (IFRS 16) · Execute mass lease accounting additions or modifications

mapHypotheses.t: Lease alert triage and journal reconciliation
mapHypotheses.d: CoStar alerts classified and pre-assigned, standard dismissals batched, and journal exports reconciled to the roll-forward before BlackLine transmission.
mapHypotheses.where: Lease Accounting (IFRS 16) · Process lease accounting entries

mapHypotheses.t: Lease self-service reporting
mapHypotheses.d: Scheduled CoStar reports published in Power BI for non-licensed users, with a request form and report catalogue for genuine ad hoc needs.
mapHypotheses.where: Lease Accounting (IFRS 16) · Execute lease accounting reporting

mapHypotheses.t: FA and lease month-end pack in Power BI
mapHypotheses.d: MOT files, CN comparison, reconciliations and project / FA reports from one data layer, with the ad hoc FA and lease views self-served; review time moves from building files to explaining movements.
mapHypotheses.feasc: Register GFA-04 self-service Power BI dashboard is tagged Not Feasible (comments: No); GFA-25 / 24 entity and country views are Feasible.
mapHypotheses.where: FA & Lease Month-End Reporting

mapHypotheses.t: One month-end data layer for FA and lease reporting
mapHypotheses.d: A single scheduled extract set (SAP asset history, GL, CoStar roll-forward) feeds the FA and lease MOT files, the CN group vs local file, the BlackLine schedules and the Power BI month-end pack - built once, reviewed by CAPEX, delivered by WD-2 / WD+4.
mapHypotheses.feasc: Register GFA-01 / 02 / 23 (Feasible): scheduled SAP extraction and SharePoint transport already run via the FC&CG framework - extend the same layer to the MOT, CN and BlackLine files.
mapHypotheses.where: FA & Lease Month-End Reporting · Prepare FA ERH MOT file

mapHypotheses.t: Write SOPs for the month-end reporting activities
mapHypotheses.d: The six month-end activities in this key process have no SOP (they come from the challenges file). Documenting them - inputs, extracts, mapping rules, review and deadlines - is the prerequisite for automating them and for cover during absence.
mapHypotheses.where: FA & Lease Month-End Reporting · Prepare and review month-end project and FA reports

stomach.name: P2P
stomach.scope: How AstraZeneca makes sure we only pay suppliers for goods and services that were ordered, received, correctly invoiced, approved and paid: the purchase order, the goods receipt and the invoice are matched in Coupa, variances are approved by the business, the liability is recorded in SAP and the payment run pays the supplier on the due date. Everything else is an exception branch or a specialist variant. Updated for the final review with Ching Yee Thow and Emily Lau (16 Oct 2026).

Daily invoice processing; scheduled payment runs; month end

mapHypotheses.t: GR ageing monitor and nudge agent
mapHypotheses.d: Monitor POs with invoices waiting in Pending receipt, nudge the requisitioner and escalate by ageing; report GR lead time by market against the P2P KPIs (Payment to Terms, Invoice TAT).
mapHypotheses.feasc: The GR reminder is already in place (Coupa notifications, email reminders, team script); the global P2P team is exploring the receipt-related AI use cases.
mapHypotheses.where: Goods & services receipt · Goods / service receipt

mapHypotheses.t: Touchless capture for unstructured invoices
mapHypotheses.d: LLM extraction and semantic matching on top of Kofax with confidence-based routing; target: most PDF and email invoices reach Coupa with no AP touch.
mapHypotheses.feasc: LLM extraction and semantic matching on top of the existing OCR - to be explored; Kofax itself is being replaced by a new global tool.
mapHypotheses.where: Invoice management · Flow 1 - Invoice received and captured (Kofax / electronic channel)

mapHypotheses.t: Exception-resolution agent for Coupa holds
mapHypotheses.d: One agent works the Draft, AP Hold, Booking Hold and Pending receipt queues: proposes the fix, chases the right person and releases within policy; AP supervises by exception.
mapHypotheses.feasc: Covered by the global non-PO project (just live), the existing Coupa notifications and the Coupa variance threshold.
mapHypotheses.where: Invoice management · Flow 2 - PO + GR + invoice match in Coupa

mapHypotheses.t: Posting-error auto-remediation
mapHypotheses.d: Classify Coupa-to-SAP posting errors, auto-apply the known fix and re-push, and feed error patterns back to DMT master-data quality.
mapHypotheses.feasc: SAP posting error messages are part of the existing design; AP investigates from the message.
mapHypotheses.where: Invoice management · Flow 3 - Approval and SAP posting

mapHypotheses.t: Payment-failure triage
mapHypotheses.d: Classify payment-run failures, pre-fill the manual payment request and track the vendor clearing (F-44) so the exception closes without re-keying.
mapHypotheses.feasc: Payment-failure handling sits with Cash & Banking (PSPC initiative) - to confirm with Cash & Banking / O2C.
mapHypotheses.where: Payment · Flow 2 - Exception: manual and emergency payments

mapHypotheses.t: Straight-through early payment requests
mapHypotheses.d: Policy-based auto-approval, approval matrix from the DOA master and automated payment-date change in SAP.
mapHypotheses.feasc: Low impact; the approval matrix part is not relevant, the SAP days update can be explored.
mapHypotheses.where: Payment · Flow 4 - Exception: early payment requests and payment date changes

mapHypotheses.t: One accrual ownership model across P2P, R2R, Controlling and FP&A Ops
mapHypotheses.rid: NPO-19 to NPO-23, NPO-27 to NPO-30
mapHypotheses.d: Agree who accrues what (pending approval vs approved-not-posted vs ad hoc vs departmental), close the Coupa AP vs Coupa P2P scope question, bring Controlling and FP&A Ops into the design, revisit the non-PO guideline as the root lever and take the continue / stop decision to local finance with the data.
mapHypotheses.feasc: TPI NPO-19 / 20 / 21 / 27: accrual ownership across the towers.
mapHypotheses.where: Month-end close

mapHypotheses.t: System-generated non-PO accruals (target Q1 2027)
mapHypotheses.d: Once the common global framework and RACI are agreed (Nov-Dec 2026), accruals are generated by the system from Coupa / Celonis data with controller review; the Python asset is the bridge until then.
mapHypotheses.feasc: TPI NPO-08: system-generated accruals from Q1 2027 once the framework and RACI are agreed.
mapHypotheses.where: Month-end close · Flow 1 - STP cut-off and non-PO accrual (APAC WD-3; China WD-6)

mapHypotheses.t: Control execution assistant
mapHypotheses.d: Runs the SOP-defined checks over scheduled extracts, drafts the control result and packages system-generated evidence for OneGRC.
mapHypotheses.where: Month-end close · Flow 2 - SOX / FCF self-assessment and reporting

mapHypotheses.t: Shared automation platform for all towers
mapHypotheses.d: The VM, repository, governance, run dashboard, coverage inventory and training pack built for P2P BSR serve O2C, Controlling and Tax too (BSR-30 feasible; BSR-31, BSR-34, BSR-35); align with the R2R-led global BSR programme and adopt what R2R has built (BSR-21, BSR-22), with GPO / GPDD endorsement (BSR-23), Genpact (BSR-27) and named regional owners (BSR-29).
mapHypotheses.rid: BSR-21 to BSR-23, BSR-27, BSR-29 to BSR-31, BSR-35
mapHypotheses.feasc: TPI BSR-30 / 31 / 32 / 35: the framework offered to all towers - feasible per the register.
mapHypotheses.where: Month-end close · Flow 3 - AP balance sheet reconciliation (BSR)

mapHypotheses.t: Down payment straight-through
mapHypotheses.d: Approved form posts the down payment, the payment run pays it and the final invoice clears it - AP confirms partial clearings only.
mapHypotheses.feasc: Coupa (Others) down payment straight-through needs a bot / integration; China already auto-posts via iPay.
mapHypotheses.where: Specialist variants (branch from the core invoice journey) · Variant 2 - Down payments and non-invoice payments

activities.d: The distributor's daily EDI sales file interfaces into AZ's SAP. SAP processes the file, creates the sales, return and rebate orders automatically and runs three checks before the order can proceed: customer, price and stock.
activities.src: O2C Sales Order team walkthrough (Oct 2026); register O2C-01.02

activities.d: The Sales Order team liaises with the Distribution team, which raises a request to DMT to create the end-customer account in SAP. SAP then re-processes the EDI order (retry).
activities.src: O2C Sales Order team walkthrough (Oct 2026); register O2C-01.02
pp: Missing end-customer accounts

activities.d: The Sales Order team asks the local market to confirm the price and GFS Controlling updates the pricing condition in SAP. SAP then re-processes the EDI order (retry).
activities.o: Sales Order team / Local market / Controlling
activities.src: O2C Sales Order team walkthrough (Oct 2026); register O2C-01.02
pp: Missing pricing

activities.d: The Sales Order team asks the Distribution team to carry out the stock movement so the order can be fulfilled. SAP then re-processes the EDI order (retry).
activities.src: O2C Sales Order team walkthrough (Oct 2026); register O2C-01.02
pp: Insufficient stock

activities.d: All three conditions are met and SAP creates the sales, return or rebate order. EDI orders are not subject to the system credit check and flow straight to billing.
activities.src: O2C Sales Order team walkthrough (Oct 2026); register O2C-01.02
out: EDI order ready to bill (no credit check)

activities.t: Receive PO, return or rebate request
activities.d: The customer sends the request directly to AZ by email or the customer portal and the Sales Order team picks it up. A purchase order is a new sale ("Dear AZ, please supply 500 units"). A return or rebate is not a sale - it is money going back to the customer: the hospital returns expired medicines, or the agreement says buy 10,000 units and get 5% back.
activities.src: O2C Sales Order team walkthrough (Oct 2026); register O2C-01.02
in: Purchase order, return or rebate claim
Return or rebate request raised by the market
activities.process: Flow 2 - Customer PO, returns and rebates (manual)

activities.t: Process Order / Credit note in SAP
activities.d: A person creates the sales order (or, for a return or rebate, the credit note) in SAP instead of SAP creating it automatically. A credit note is a negative invoice: the invoice said the customer owes AZ RM10,000; the credit note says AZ owes the customer RM1,000. SAP then checks the credit limit.
activities.src: O2C Sales Order team walkthrough (Oct 2026); register O2C-01.02
pp: Manual order creation
Missing customer accounts
Missing pricing
Incorrect VAT setup
activities.ci: Completed: Python script automates Alexion order processing, returns and rebates. WIP: Global CN dashboard
activities.ctl: Approval checks for EDI credit notes, manual credit notes and non-standard orders (sample, FOC zero value)
activities.process: Flow 2 - Customer PO, returns and rebates (manual)

activities.t: System credit check on manual orders
activities.d: Every manual order (not EDI) goes through the SAP credit check. SAP blocks the order if the customer's credit limit is exceeded, the account has an overdue balance, or the payment term has changed. The Order Release team works the blocked-orders list daily.
activities.src: O2C Sales Order team walkthrough (Oct 2026); register O2C-01.02; register O2C-01.03
pp: High volume of order blocks in CNXX markets
activities.ci: WIP: system change to exclude Banker's Acceptance from the CNXX credit exposure (go-live Q4 2026)

activities.d: The Credit Risk team reviews the exposure and obtains the approval required under GDOA 2002, then passes the evidenced approval to the Order Release team for release.
activities.src: O2C Sales Order team walkthrough (Oct 2026); register O2C-01.02; register O2C-01.03

activities.d: The Collection team reviews the overdue position and obtains approval in accordance with the Global Credit Risk Policy, then passes it to the Order Release team for release.
activities.src: O2C Sales Order team walkthrough (Oct 2026); register O2C-01.02; register O2C-01.03

activities.d: The Credit Risk team reviews the payment-term change and obtains approval in accordance with GDOA 2000, then passes it to the Order Release team for release.
activities.src: O2C Sales Order team walkthrough (Oct 2026); register O2C-01.02; register O2C-01.03

activities.d: The Order Release team releases the blocked order once the appropriate approval is evidenced. The released order goes to Distribution for delivery (goods issue) and then to Billing.
activities.src: O2C Sales Order team walkthrough (Oct 2026); register O2C-01.02; register O2C-01.03
activities.ctl: Approval check for order block release

activities.t: PGI posting based on delivery to customer
activities.d: Delivery of the stock to the customer triggers the post goods issue (PGI) in SAP, which posts the COGS. The Billing team checks the posting against the delivery.
activities.src: O2C Sales Order team walkthrough (Oct 2026); register O2C-01.02; register O2C-01.06

activities.d: The Billing team releases billing in SAP so revenue is recognised.
activities.src: O2C Sales Order team walkthrough (Oct 2026); register O2C-01.02; register O2C-01.06

activities.d: Invoices and credit notes are generated in SAP. Country-specific compliance (local tax invoice, e-invoicing) may still be needed before the invoice is complete and billed to the customer. An incorrect VAT classification in the master data shows up here as an inaccurate invoice.
activities.src: O2C Sales Order team walkthrough (Oct 2026); register O2C-01.02; register O2C-01.06
pp: Incorrect VAT classification in master data gives inaccurate invoices

tpis.t: Correct the initial payroll posting at source
tpis.act: Split the P1 payroll interface so actual payments post to the bank-clearing GL and payment holds post directly to GL 23110100, eliminating the initial corrective journal.

tpis.t: Create and map a payment-hold wage type
tpis.act: Request the payroll service provider to create a dedicated payment-hold wage type and map it to GL 23110100 for GBS HR-supported markets.
tpis.xt: Yes — O2C/Payroll, People Services/GBS, payroll provider: Create and map a payment-hold wage type.

tpis.t: Secure cost approval for wage-type creation
tpis.act: Prepare and approve the change cost so the service provider can configure and test the new wage type without delaying the posting correction.

tpis.t: Align non-GBS markets with local stakeholders
tpis.act: For TW, TH, VN, KR and HK, use Controlling and local HR/Finance engagement to agree the corrected posting treatment and market-specific implementation steps.
tpis.xt: Yes — O2C/Payroll, Controlling/R2R, local HR/Finance: Align non-GBS markets with local stakeholders.

tpis.t: Govern the phased market rollout
tpis.act: Maintain a market plan covering wage-type setup, GL mapping, testing, sign-off and milestones; use Q3/Q4 dates where agreed and flag markets without a confirmed timeline.
tpis.xt: Yes — O2C/Payroll, Controlling/R2R, local HR/Finance: Govern the phased market rollout.
tpis.st: Can be implemented in the future
tpis.sr: Can be implemented in the future

tpis.t: Include the release journal in a subsequent payroll posting
tpis.act: Assess whether the payment-release reclassification can be included in the following payroll cycle so a separate month-end journal is removed while the release remains traceable.
tpis.xt: Yes — O2C/Payroll, R2R, Controlling: Include the release journal in a subsequent payroll posting.

tpis.t: Correct-first-entry release posting using employee and hold references
tpis.act: Explore posting the payroll release correctly in the payroll upload using Employee ID and hold month, with a direct link to the original held amount and GL 23110100.
tpis.xt: Yes — O2C/Payroll, FP&A Ops, People Services/GBS, Controlling/R2R: Correct-first-entry release posting using employee and hold references.

tpis.t: Automate the release reclassification to bank GL
tpis.act: If source-system release posting cannot be corrected immediately, use a controlled rules-based journal workflow to create the bank-GL reclassification from approved release events.
tpis.xt: Yes — O2C/Payroll, FP&A Comm, Controlling/R2R: Automate the release reclassification to bank GL.

tpis.t: Hold-to-release control and data specification
tpis.act: Define one event model covering hold creation, release instruction, employee reference, hold month, posting account and release status before configuration or automation begins.
tpis.xt: Yes — O2C/Payroll, Controlling/R2R, People Services/GBS, payroll provider: Hold-to-release control and data specification.

tpis.t: Payroll exception dashboard
tpis.act: Provide a read-only control view of unreleased holds, ageing, bank-GL mismatches, release status and journal completion so finance teams can work from one reconciled exception list.
tpis.xt: Yes — Controlling/R2R, O2C/Payroll, FP&A Ops, FP&A Comm: Payroll exception dashboard.
tpis.st: Can be implemented in the future
tpis.sr: Can be implemented in the future

tpis.t: Reusable payroll interface validation
tpis.act: Automate deterministic checks that actual payment equals the bank posting, held amounts equal the accrual posting and every release links to the original hold.
tpis.xt: Yes — O2C/Payroll, R2R, Controlling: Reusable payroll interface validation.

tpis.t: Market rollout control pack
tpis.act: Use one controlled pack for wage-type setup, GL mapping, cost approval, test evidence, owner sign-off and milestone tracking across GBS and non-GBS markets.
tpis.xt: Yes — O2C/Payroll, Controlling/R2R, local HR/Finance: Market rollout control pack.

tpis.t: AI-generated payroll exception summary
tpis.act: After stable history exists, draft a month-end summary of aged holds, repeated release failures and reconciliation themes for reviewer action only.

tpis.t: Automated wage-type and GL regression testing

tpis.t: Automated hold-to-release event matching

mapHypotheses.t: Order-to-invoice exception dashboard by market and cause
mapHypotheses.d: Bring EDI errors, manual-order exceptions and order blocks from SAP into one Power BI view by market, customer and root cause (account, price, stock, VAT, credit) so the Sales Order, Credit Risk and Billing teams fix master data and credit settings instead of case-by-case follow-up.
mapHypotheses.where: Sales order creation

mapHypotheses.t: Auto-triage EDI order errors to the resolving team
mapHypotheses.d: A scheduled script extracts the daily EDI order error log from SAP, classifies each error (missing end-customer account, missing price, insufficient stock) and raises it to DMT / Distribution, the market and Controlling, or Distribution with a tracked status - replacing email follow-up by the Sales Order team.
mapHypotheses.where: Sales order creation · Flow 1 - EDI orders (automatic)

mapHypotheses.t: Pre-creation master-data validation (customer, price, VAT)
mapHypotheses.d: Before an order or credit note is created, check the customer account status, price condition and VAT classification against SAP master data and flag mismatches to DMT, stopping incorrect VAT at source rather than at the invoice.
mapHypotheses.feas: Can be explored & in progress for VAT Validation Only
mapHypotheses.feasc: GFS Innovation team working on a pilot for Philippines market
mapHypotheses.where: Sales order creation · Flow 2 - Customer PO, returns and rebates (manual)

mapHypotheses.t: Predictive credit-block reduction for CNXX markets
mapHypotheses.d: Use twelve months of block, release and payment history to recommend credit-limit adjustments for customers repeatedly blocked but paying on time, for Credit Risk approval - reducing the volume of blocks at source alongside the Banker's Acceptance exclusion.
mapHypotheses.where: Order block release

mapHypotheses.t: Release-on-approval workflow with evidence trail
mapHypotheses.d: One workflow for the three block reasons: the blocked order generates the approval request with the exposure summary, routes it to the GDOA 2002 / Credit Risk Policy / GDOA 2000 approver, stores the evidence and triggers the SAP release by script.
mapHypotheses.where: Order block release · Order block release (manual orders)

mapHypotheses.t: E-invoice submission and status monitoring
mapHypotheses.d: Automatic submission of SAP billing data to each mandated tax-authority portal, status write-back to SAP and a rejection queue by market, so new e-invoicing mandates are onboarded as configuration rather than new manual steps.
mapHypotheses.where: Billing · Billing (invoices, credit notes, e-invoicing)

mapHypotheses.t: Overpayment and refund tracker (China aged overpayments)
mapHypotheses.d: Age customer overpayments in High Radius / SAP, trigger the refund request to Cash & Banking once the market criteria are met and report aged balances by customer, replacing manual follow-up of China overpayments.
mapHypotheses.where: Collections & disputes management

mapHypotheses.t: Predictive payment-risk scoring
mapHypotheses.d: Score open invoices by likelihood of late payment from High Radius history (customer, market, past commitments kept) to focus pre-due calls on the invoices most at risk and recommend when to escalate.
mapHypotheses.where: Collections & disputes management · Collection - payment follow-up and escalation

mapHypotheses.t: Deduction-to-credit-note matching
mapHypotheses.d: Match customer deductions taken on payment to open or approved claims (returns, rebates, AP-due invoices) before the credit note is issued, so valid deductions clear on posting and invalid ones return to collections with the evidence attached.
mapHypotheses.where: Collections & disputes management · Disputes and deductions management

mapHypotheses.t: Auto-match rate monitoring by market and unmatched reason
mapHypotheses.d: A Power BI view of the High Radius auto-match rate by market and the reason for each unmatched payment (no remittance, lump sum, advance, short-pay) so rule tuning and customer remittance requests target the biggest causes.
mapHypotheses.where: Payment allocation / cash application · Payment allocation - matched payments

mapHypotheses.t: Payment-to-bank-to-ledger reconciliation
mapHypotheses.d: Match each payment request, payment instruction, bank confirmation and accounting entry automatically and route only the breaks for investigation - covering the automated run, manual payments and the bank statement in one control.
mapHypotheses.where: Cash & Banking

mapHypotheses.t: Pre-payment beneficiary and duplicate validation
mapHypotheses.d: Validate beneficiary bank details, currency, amount limits and approver authority against governed masters and check for duplicate payments before the file is released, so rejections and re-issues fall at source.
mapHypotheses.where: Cash & Banking · Flow A - Payment process: automated / semi-automated payment run

mapHypotheses.t: Manual payment status and exception dashboard
mapHypotheses.d: Show each Crown request's age, approval stage, payment status, cut-off risk and rejection reason in one view for the Cash & Banking team and requesters, replacing status emails.
mapHypotheses.where: Cash & Banking · Flow A - Payment process: manual payment route

mapHypotheses.t: Open-item ageing and ownership dashboard
mapHypotheses.d: One reconciled list of bank open items by category, stakeholder, age and status (payroll, T&E, vendor refunds, unidentified) so the follow-up is worked from a single view and aged items are visible before month-end.
mapHypotheses.rid: O2C-03.02 - TPI register PAY-10 pattern applied to bank open items
mapHypotheses.where: Cash & Banking · Flow B - Bank statement process

mapHypotheses.t: WHT engine from invoice to certificate
mapHypotheses.d: Vendor tax rules, service classification, WHT determination, treaty validation and exception routing before posting, feeding the monthly payment file, the annual return and WHT certificates from the same calculation data - the Miro future state (Aug 2026).
mapHypotheses.where: Withholding Tax (Australia)

mapHypotheses.t: WHT determination assistant at invoice capture
mapHypotheses.d: Classify the vendor, service and treaty position at invoice capture, propose the WHT code and rate with a reason code, and route exceptions to TDT - the preventive validation the SOP currently assumes rather than checks.
mapHypotheses.where: Withholding Tax (Australia) · Phase 3 - WHT review and posting

mapHypotheses.t: Monthly WHT remittance pack built unattended
mapHypotheses.d: WD+2 extract, reversal and prior-month filter, payment file, FC approval and CROWN request chained into one scheduled flow with TDT reviewing the exceptions and the total.
mapHypotheses.where: Withholding Tax (Australia) · Phase 5 - Monthly WHT remittance

mapHypotheses.t: Annual WHT return assembled from the monthly files
mapHypotheses.d: Annual listing, reconciliation to the twelve payment files, vendor details and the form fields produced by script; FC review and CFO signature captured in one approval with the lodgement route confirmed with the ATO.
mapHypotheses.where: Withholding Tax (Australia) · Phase 6 - Annual WHT filing

mapHypotheses.t: Tax GL Analyzer as the CIT pack engine, piloted end-to-end in one market
mapHypotheses.d: Group IT builds from Tax-supplied rules (TAX-17), fed by the R2R fixed asset, vendor and cost centre data (TAX-19, TAX-20), scaled across categories and regions (TAX-02, TAX-03) and taken to a drafted computation for a pilot market shown to Group Tax (TAX-15, TAX-21).
mapHypotheses.where: Corporate Income Tax (Australia AU10)

mapHypotheses.t: Tax GL Analyzer scaled to the full CIT pack with AI on the unclassified lines
mapHypotheses.d: Rule-based analyzer across all CIT pack categories (TAX-02) with AI summarising and categorising the 'requires human analysis' lines (TAX-04), proposing rule updates for approval (TAX-05), run as a scheduled chain prompt for consistent output (TAX-11, TAX-12).
mapHypotheses.where: Corporate Income Tax (Australia AU10) · Phase 3 - Tax data and local adjustments

mapHypotheses.t: Flux commentary and trend assistant
mapHypotheses.d: Draft the flux commentary and surface trends from the analysed GL population (TAX-07) for the TDT, Financial Controller and Deloitte review, with the review template populated automatically.
mapHypotheses.where: Corporate Income Tax (Australia AU10) · Phase 4 - Computation and review

mapHypotheses.t: Tax balance reconciliation monitor
mapHypotheses.d: Monthly scripted reconciliation of the corporate tax receivable and payable GLs with ageing by tax year, refunds matched to returns, extended to VAT and WHT payable GLs.
mapHypotheses.where: Corporate Income Tax (Australia AU10) · Phase 7 - Post-filing and reporting

mapHypotheses.t: Single VAT data-to-return pipeline
mapHypotheses.d: Flags at posting, scheduled extraction and FPT download, automated upload to Intela, e-invoice reconciliation and an approval flow that marks the return complete in Intela and pre-fills the CROWN payment.
mapHypotheses.where: VAT (Vietnam)

mapHypotheses.t: Input VAT validity flags at posting
mapHypotheses.d: PENDING, reversal / correction and sponsorship lines flagged once at posting so the monthly return review starts from a classified ledger.
mapHypotheses.where: VAT (Vietnam) · Phase 2 - Transaction processing and VAT posting

mapHypotheses.t: Scheduled VAT data pack to Intela
mapHypotheses.d: SAP extracts, FPT reports and the sum-netting report collected by scheduled scripts, uploaded to the Intela information request and Deloitte Vietnam notified without the macro workbook or manual fallback.
mapHypotheses.where: VAT (Vietnam) · Phase 4 - VAT data gathering

mapHypotheses.t: E-invoice to SAP output VAT reconciliation
mapHypotheses.d: Reconcile FPT e-invoices to SAP output VAT and present the exceptions and pre-flagged items to TDT, so the review of Deloitte's draft focuses on judgement items.
mapHypotheses.where: VAT (Vietnam) · Phase 5 - Return preparation and review

mapHypotheses.t: Group tax reporting workbench for TDT
mapHypotheses.d: One place for the quarterly TRT input, the RTP loads and tie-outs, the Group Tax threshold flags and the pushdown journal pack, replacing the mix of TRT screens, Excel mapping tables and email confirmations.
mapHypotheses.where: Group Tax Reporting (Tier 3 and 4 entities)

mapHypotheses.t: TRT input assistant for Tier 3 and 4
mapHypotheses.d: NA1201 pre-populated from the prior RTP and NA1101, review checklist and questionnaire in a Power App, and the quarterly confirmation to Group Tax generated from it.
mapHypotheses.where: Group Tax Reporting (Tier 3 and 4 entities) · Flow 1 - Quarterly CIT reporting calculation in the TRT

mapHypotheses.t: RTP tie-out and threshold checker
mapHypotheses.d: Load the RTP template tables into the TRT by script, tie out to the TARF, NA1602 and NA1301 reports and raise the Group Tax threshold flags automatically.
mapHypotheses.where: Group Tax Reporting (Tier 3 and 4 entities) · Flow 2 - Prior year adjustments (RTP) into the TRT

mapHypotheses.t: Pushdown journal pack from the TRT
mapHypotheses.d: One scheduled run after the Briefing Note: journal and TARF exports per entity, local finance approval flow, BlackLine template pre-filled and the SAP-to-TARF reconciliation by script.
mapHypotheses.where: Group Tax Reporting (Tier 3 and 4 entities) · Flow 3 - SAP pushdown of CIT reporting balances (8.6.1.95)

kidneys.name: Controlling
kidneys.scope: Two questions for the visitor: how does GFS Controlling make sure every judgmental manual journal posted in the month-end close is needed, GSOP-compliant, approved and reviewed in the management P&L, and how does it get the statutory audit from planning to filed accounts across all the process towers each year? The answer is the journey below - the Business requests, Embedded Finance approves the cost, the GFS Controller checks the GSOP and posts in BlackLine, the GFS Manager approves and GFS FP&A reviews the P&L; the audit runs from planning and walkthroughs through PBC evidence, fieldwork, financial statement review and P13 adjustments to statutory filing. Pain points and TPI 2026 initiatives are shown where Controlling recorded them.
meta: GFS Controlling (Embedded Finance CFO / FC / CBP, GFS Controller, GFS Manager) with Business requestors, GFS FP&A, Tax, all process towers and the auditors (KPMG / Deloitte)
MJV: monthly, during the month-end close before the WD+2 GL close · Statutory audit: annual cycle
Email (requests) · BlackLine (journal preparation, approval, posting) · SAP (postings, P13) · KPMG Clara / KCC (PBC evidence) · Wdesk / Workiva (financial statement review)

mapHypotheses.t: Governed journal pipeline: request form → validation → BlackLine → dashboard, scaled across towers
mapHypotheses.d: One intake form, one validation service, root cause captured at posting and one governed journal dataset published for every team posting through BlackLine (MJV-10), with natural-language Q&A over the journal history for authorised users (MJV-18).
mapHypotheses.feasc: Register MJV-10 scale the dashboard across towers: can be implemented in the future; MJV-18: AI-suggested, to be reviewed.
mapHypotheses.where: Manual Journal Preparation (MJV)

mapHypotheses.t: Preventable journal elimination loop
mapHypotheses.d: Dashboard (MJV-01) identifies the highest-volume requestors and causes (MJV-08); each preventable cause gets an accountable upstream owner and due date (MJV-05); benefits and recurrence are tracked automatically (MJV-21) and reviewed with CFOs monthly and AA leadership quarterly (MJV-09) - the mechanism behind the 30 percent MJV reduction target.
mapHypotheses.feasc: Register MJV-05 / 08 / 09: can be implemented in the future; MJV-21 automated benefit and recurrence tracking: AI-suggested, to be reviewed.
mapHypotheses.where: Manual Journal Preparation (MJV) · Manual Journal Request (MJV)

mapHypotheses.t: Audit-to-close feedback loop
mapHypotheses.d: Recurring findings and clarification reasons (AUD-13), audit-adjustment clusters (AUD-19) and the early-risk log (AUD-08) feed the MJV prevention backlog and the tower SOPs, so the statutory audit improves the next close instead of only reporting on the last one.
mapHypotheses.feasc: Register AUD-13: status blank - Controlling asked for further explanation (data held in KPMG KCC); AUD-19: AI-suggested, to be reviewed; AUD-08: can be implemented in the future.
mapHypotheses.where: Statutory Audit

mapHypotheses.t: Reusable evidence-extraction factory
mapHypotheses.d: The PH10 SAP extraction script assessed as a reusable pattern, then approved Coupa / API routes, standard manifests and found / missing / failed logs added for the other evidence types (AUD-10) - so each tower produces its PBC population in one run instead of one-by-one downloads.
mapHypotheses.feasc: Register AUD-10: status blank - Controlling asked for further explanation; kept Under review.
mapHypotheses.where: Statutory Audit · Statutory audit end-to-end (seven sub-processes)
